Attachment.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

AttachmentSpec.description: Attaching is its own object, so a crash mid-way leaves a truthful record rather than a volume nobody can reattach.

node.description: The name of a `nodes` object. Where the volume will be opened. Taken from the instance. Derived: omitted, the API fills it in; stated, it must agree.

AuditRecord.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

AuditRecordSpec.description: What was refused, and who signed in. Not a log of everything that happened — every successful write already leaves an operation carrying its target, its verb and who asked. What no operation exists for is a request that was turned down, and that is the one a multi-tenant cell gets asked about later.

BGPPeer.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

BGPPeerSpec.description: Sessions from the cell's gateways to the routers in front of it. What gets announced is derived, never listed: every external subnet, and a host route for each public address that is in front of something — so the router ahead of the cell and this console cannot disagree about what the cell claims.

multihop.description: Only when the router is not on the same wire: eBGP refuses a neighbour more than one hop away unless told the distance.

node.description: The name of a `nodes` object. The machine that holds the session — a gateway, with FRR installed. One session is one speaker.

password.description: The same string the router has for this session (RFC 2385). Most firewalls will not bring a session up without one.

peer.description: The router or firewall in front of the cell.

Backup.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

BackupSchedule.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

BackupScheduleSpec.description: An intention, not a job queue: there should be a copy of this volume no older than the interval, and the last few kept. What exists is what decides — a copy still being made holds the schedule, and a stuck one holds it for one interval and no longer.

everyHours.description: How stale the newest copy may get before another is made. An interval rather than a cron line, because the only question anybody asks a schedule is when it will next run.

keep.description: How many of this schedule's copies to keep. Only finished copies count, so a run of failures never expires the last one that worked. Copies taken by hand are never expired.

target.description: The name of a `backup-targets` object. Where the copies go.

volume.description: The name of a `volumes` object. What is copied.

BackupSpec.description: One copy of one volume, at one moment. Restoring makes a new volume from a copy — never writing one back over the original, which would be a command living in a spec and carried out again on every resync.

target.description: The name of a `backup-targets` object. Where the copy goes. Left empty, the cell's most roomy accepting target answers. A target in the volume's own pool is refused: a copy beside the original is a snapshot, and is lost with the pool it is in.

volume.description: The name of a `volumes` object. What is copied.

BackupTarget.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

BackupTargetSpec.description: Where backups are kept. Deliberately not a pool: a copy that lives beside the original is a snapshot, and is lost with the pool it is in. A target in a volume's own pool is refused.

accepting.description: Turning this off stops new copies going here. What is already here stays, and can still be restored from.

agent.description: The name of a `pools` object. The pool agent that says whether this path is there, whether it can be written, and how much room is left. Named rather than claimed by whoever gets there first — a target assigned to nobody is one any agent could report on. Leave it empty and nobody looks: copies are still written by the pool holding the volume, and a path it cannot reach fails on the backup instead.

path.description: An absolute path the agent can already write to. Mounting an NFS or CIFS share is the host's job, not this platform's — one that managed its own mounts would be a second, worse copy of what init already does.

verifyEveryHours.description: How often a copy here is read back and checked against what it hashed to when it was written. 0 never checks, which is the default: verification reads every byte of a copy, and that is real I/O somebody has to decide to spend. Without it, 'the backup exists' is the only thing anybody can say about it. One copy per pass, the one whose last check is stalest — so a target holding more copies checks each of them less often rather than falling behind on the work that is not optional.

Capture.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

CaptureSpec.description: Build a guest by hand, get it right, capture it — then every guest made from the result starts where that one left off. The guest must be stopped: a disk copied from under a running machine is crash-consistent, and a template is stamped out by people who assume it is clean.

instance.description: The name of a `instances` object. It must be stopped. A disk copied from under a running machine is crash-consistent, which a template stamped out a hundred times must not be — if you want a copy of a live guest, take a backup instead.

label.description: What the resulting image is called. Its digest is added to this — a list of hashes is not something anybody chooses from.

target.description: The name of a `backup-targets` object. Where the bytes go. Any node that can reach the same path can then boot guests from the image.

CephCluster.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

CephClusterSpec.description: Cluster storage every node reaches, instead of a pool per machine. Optional: a cell with directory pools is a working cell, and nothing here turns itself on. Choosing a disk for an OSD erases it.

clusterNetwork.description: A separate network for replication. Empty means the one above carries both, which is the ordinary answer for a small cluster.

monitors.description: Three nodes, or one for a lab. Never two: a quorum of two survives no failures and looks like it would.

osds.description: One disk, one OSD. Anything that cannot be chosen says why beside it rather than being greyed out — only a device the node can see is empty is offered, so a disk you really do want to give up has to be wiped outside the platform first.

paused.description: Stops the deployment where it stands. Nothing is torn down, and turning it off carries on from there.

pools.description: Where volumes are stored. Copies is how many of every object exist; below the floor the pool refuses writes rather than holding data it cannot protect — so a floor equal to the copies means one node rebooting stops writing.

publicNetwork.description: Where the daemons talk to each other and to clients. A node with several interfaces has several answers, and the wrong one puts replication traffic on the tenant network.

reason.description: One word in CamelCase, for a program.

ConsoleSession.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

ConsoleSessionSpec.description: The console has no form for this collection, so its fields are not enumerated here; docs/rest-contract.md names them.

DeviceClass.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

DeviceClassSpec.description: Names for interchangeable hardware. An instance asks for a class, never an address: an address belongs to one machine, so an instance naming one could only ever run there. A device is offered only when everything in its IOMMU group is free — a group is passed through whole or not at all.

description.description: What to call it in this console.

matches.description: vendor:device, as `lspci -n` prints it. Several, because a fleet buys the same accelerator across board revisions.

field.description: The offending path, `spec.vcpus`, when there is one.

Flavor.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

FlavorSpec.description: Named machine sizes, offered by the cell. A guest is an                 m1-small, not a hand-entered triple of numbers — the sizes that                 land on the fleet are the shapes it was bought for. Whether a                 project may also size by hand is that project's policy.

description.description: One sentence for the picker. The numbers already say most of it.

FloatingIP.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

FloatingIPSpec.description: Addresses that outlive the machine answering on them. The address is held by the declaration, not by the port, so replacing a guest does not change what the outside world reaches.

address.description: Leave empty to be given the lowest address nothing else holds.

announce.description: The machine holding the guest is the shortest path: nothing is encapsulated for traffic to and from the world, and the route follows a live migration by itself. It needs every hypervisor to be allowed to peer with the router above it. A gateway node needs only that one machine to peer, and costs a detour in both directions.

delivery.description: Held by the guest means the address is bound to its port and configured inside the machine — nothing rewrites a packet, and the guest can tell anybody its own address, which SIP, FTP, IPsec and mDNS all need. Translated means the edge answers for it and the guest never knows. A held address has to come from an external network.

instance.description: The name of a `instances` object. The guest this address sits in front of. Its interface and the cell's public pool are found for you — name the subnet under More settings to choose v6, or a particular pool. Settable at creation only.

port.description: The name of a `ports` object. The port this address reaches. Clearing it holds the address while the machine behind it is replaced.

subnet.description: The name of a `subnets` object. Where the address comes from. Left empty, the cell's public pool answers — IPv4 first. Naming a subnet is how you choose v6, or a particular pool.

Folder.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

FolderSpec.description: A place to put projects, and a place to grant a role once instead of forty times. Roles granted here reach everything below.

parent.description: The name of a `folders` object. Left empty this folder sits at the top. Roles granted above it reach in here too.

Image.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

ImageSource.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

ImageSourceSpec.description: Where a family's images come from. The cell asks the checksums file what the current digest is, over https so the certificate is checked, and publishes an image when the answer is one it does not have. Nothing about a running guest changes: a machine keeps the bytes it was built from, and "always the newest" means new machines get it.

checksums.description: A `sha256sum`-style file covering the image's filename. **https only**, and refused otherwise — this is the one value the whole arrangement trusts, and whoever can rewrite it chooses what every new guest in this cell boots.

everyMs.description: Six hours when left empty. Cloud images are published daily at best, and a cell that asks every minute spends its day fetching a checksums file to learn nothing.

family.description: Everything this source publishes joins this family, and an instance asking for `families/debian-13` gets the newest of them.

keep.description: How many of this family to keep. Three when left empty. An image an instance was built from is never taken away, however old — the guest would be unable to start on its next move.

paused.description: Stop looking, without forgetting where this came from.

url.description: Where the bytes are. This may be plain http: the digest below is what makes fetching them safe, and a wrong byte gives a wrong digest and fails the fetch.

ImageSpec.description: Content-addressed and immutable. Cached copies are a placement preference, never a requirement.

digest.description: The bytes are addressed by this, so an image cannot be replaced under an instance that was built from it.

family.description: What this image is, in the words somebody would use to ask for it. An instance can then name `families/debian-13` and get the newest one there is, resolved when it is created and written down — so a guest never changes its operating system on a restart.

from.description: The name of a `images` object. Take the digest, format, size and source from an image that already exists. Nothing is copied — an image is addressed by its digest, so every node that had the bytes still has them. Anything you fill in below wins over what is taken. Settable at creation only.

signature.description: An Ed25519 signature over `sha256:<digest>`, base64. Accepted only when it verifies under a key the cell was started with; refused otherwise, so a stored signature is a verified one.

version.description: Which one in the family, for a person to read. Newest is decided by when this cell learned of the image, not by comparing this — every scheme for ordering version strings is wrong for somebody's.

Instance.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

InstanceSpec.description: Guests. What was asked for is the spec; what the node reports is the status, and they are shown together.

console.description: Publishes what the guest writes to its serial console, so it can be read here. Off by default because it costs a report every time the guest logs a line. A guest that is not running shows its last output whether this is on or not.

desiredState.description: What it should be doing. Asking twice is the same as asking once.

devices.description: A class, not a machine's address. Two of the same class means two devices. A guest holding one cannot be live-migrated — a device's state is in hardware and cannot be transferred.

flavor.description: The name of a `flavors` object. A named size from the cell's menu. Picking one sets the vCPUs,                memory and root disk below; typing sizes instead needs the                project's leave.

image.description: The name of a `families` object. The newest of the family, resolved once when the machine is made. An existing machine keeps the bytes it was built from. Settable at creation only.

networks.description: Left empty, this guest joins your project's default network — made the first time somebody needs it, so two machines in a project can talk without anybody configuring anything. Settable at creation only.

node.description: The name of a `nodes` object. Left empty the scheduler chooses. Moving it afterwards is a migration, not an edit.

onNodeLoss.description: Only for a guest whose storage every node can reach. One on local storage that is started elsewhere is an empty machine wearing a familiar name. Nothing is moved until the node has been quiet long enough that its own agent has certainly stopped its guests — a node with no fencing deadline is never recovered from.

placementPolicy.affinity.description: A rule refuses every node but the one the group is already on, and says which that is. A wish places elsewhere rather than not at all.

placementPolicy.affinityGroup.description: The opposite ask: instances in one group are placed together. For a pair that talks constantly — an application and the cache it reads on every request — where a hop between machines is the whole latency budget.

placementPolicy.antiAffinityGroup.description: Instances in one group are kept off the same node — what keeps a service alive when a machine dies.

placementPolicy.minCpuLevel.description: What the image needs to run. RHEL 9 and CentOS Stream 9 need x86-64-v2 or they will not boot.

placementPolicy.requiredLabels.description: Only nodes carrying all of these.

placementPolicy.spread.description: A rule refuses a node that already runs a member — three replicas of a database must not share a machine even if that means one stays down. A wish takes a crowded node over not running at all, which is what twelve web servers want.

ports.description: For a NIC that already exists — one holding an address you want this guest to keep. To simply put a machine on a network, name the network above and the port is made for you.

rootDiskGib.description: Set by the flavor when one is picked.

sshKeys.description: Read by cloud-init on the guest's **first** boot and never again, so adding one to a machine that has already started does nothing to that machine. Without a key and without a password set in user-data, the console is the only way in.

startDelayS.description: Measured from the newest start in that group, not each member in turn — a hundred guests at thirty seconds each would be fifty minutes of nothing happening.

startOrder.description: Lower starts first; the same number is a group that starts together. Matters after a power cut, when a node brings back everything it holds at once and the database loses the race for disk to a dozen web servers.

userData.description: Handed to the guest on first boot.

volumes.description: Attached once the guest is on a node. Take one off the list to detach it.

LoadBalancer.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

LoadBalancerSpec.description: One address in front of many ports. The fabric balances by connection on whichever host traffic arrives at — there is no appliance to place and nothing to fail over. Nothing here probes a member's health: the pool is what was declared, not a judgement about it.

listeners.description: The ports the address answers on. Traffic is spread across the pool by connection, so one client's connection stays on one member.

members.description: The ports behind the address — ports, not addresses, so a migrated guest stays in the pool. Empty holds the address and forwards to nothing.

network.description: The name of a `networks` object. The network the address lives on. It scopes the service, so two projects may front the same address on different networks.

subnet.description: The name of a `subnets` object. Where the address comes from. The same counting as a port's address and a floating IP's, so no two of them are ever the same address.

vip.description: Leave empty to be given the lowest address nothing else holds.

MaintenanceWindow.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

MaintenanceWindowSpec.description: Say in advance that a machine is going out of service, and the cell stops placing work on it when the time comes — without anybody being awake to flip a switch, and without anything to flip back afterwards. Whether a window is upcoming, open or over is read off the clock, so a window that ends puts everything back by ceasing to be open.

drain.description: Off — nothing new is placed here and everything already running stays put, which is what a four-minute firmware update wants. On — the guests are migrated away as well, which is what pulling the machine wants. A guest that cannot move is left where it is, and :explainMaintenance says which.

minutes.description: How long it stays open. There is no end time to keep in step with this one: two fields that can disagree about the same fact are one field too many.

node.description: The name of a `nodes` object. The machine going out of service.

note.description: Shown wherever this window is the reason something was refused, so "no capacity" reads as "node-b is out until 03:00 for the memory swap" instead.

startsAt.description: A moment, as milliseconds since the Unix epoch. In your own timezone. A start already past means now — work that has already begun is a true thing to declare.

generation.description: Bumped on every change to spec.

revision.description: The store revision; what `If-Match` and `fromRevision` carry.

Migration.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

MigrationSpec.description: Moving a running guest to another node. There is no migrating state anywhere: this object is the ask, and whether it is finished is read from where the instance actually runs. Start one from the instance you want to move — the destination is chosen where the guest is.

connections.description: Parallel streams for the transfer. One is the only value a local socket accepts.

downtimeMs.description: The pause the guest may take at the end. A busy guest needs a larger budget or the transfer never converges.

fromNode.description: The name of a `nodes` object. Where the guest is now. Taken from the instance. Derived: omitted, the API fills it in; stated, it must agree.

mode.description: What a failure costs. Under Live the guest stays where it is; under Post-copy a failure mid-flight loses it.

timeoutS.description: A migration that cannot converge is one that runs until somebody notices.

toNode.description: The name of a `nodes` object. Only the nodes that can receive this guest can be chosen. The rest are shown with the reason they cannot.

Network.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

NetworkSpec.description: One VNI on the fabric. The nodes that have it programmed are on the object.

announce.description: What this cell does by default for addresses from this network. An individual address may say otherwise. Meaningless on a network that carries no real addresses.

external.description: The prefixes on this network's subnets are routed to this cell by whoever is above it, so an address from one is an address the world can reach. Only a cell operator may say so — a tenant who could would mint themselves a public range by typing a CIDR.

hostBridge.description: A bridge that already exists on the nodes — `br0`, `vmbr0`. Guests on this network go straight onto whatever the machine is on: the house LAN, a VLAN, a lab network. Their addresses come from whatever serves that wire and this platform allocates none, holds no gateway and enforces no security group. Empty is the ordinary case. Only a cell operator may set it — it is a decision about the machine, not about a project. Settable at creation only.

mtu.description:
1450 when left empty: a VXLAN header is 50 bytes, and a tenant \
               network handed the wire's own 1500 black-holes every large packet \
               in a way that looks like an application bug for a week.

vni.description:
The VXLAN network identifier. Left empty, the cell assigns the \
               smallest free one — which is the only correct answer, and not one \
               a tenant can work out. Derived: omitted, the API fills it in; stated, it must agree.

Node.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

NodeSpec.description: Hypervisors. The spec is what an operator decided about one; the status is what its agent last reported. Adding one here creates the object and mints its registration token — shown once, because the platform keeps a hash and cannot show it again.

cpuBaseline.description: Present the same CPU as other nodes so guests can migrate between them. Guests already running keep the CPU they started with and adopt this one when they next restart.

evacuate.description: Separate from draining. Draining says nothing new comes here; this says none of the old stays either. One migration is started per guest that can move — a guest holding a passed-through device cannot, and stays with the reason on it.

fenceAfterS.description: How long this node may fail to report before it stops the guests it holds. Zero means it never does — and a node that never does is never recovered from, because nothing can tell "unreachable" from "stopped". Set it and guests marked for restart can be brought up elsewhere.

gateway.description: A public address whose network says so is announced from here, and packets for it reach the guest over the overlay. Several machines may carry it — the network above sees them as equal next hops — and a cell with none simply cannot use that mode.

schedulable.description: Turning this off drains the node: nothing new is placed, what runs keeps running.

vcpuOvercommit.description: How many vCPUs this machine may hand out per real core. Zero or one means one for one. A processor can be shared — two guests that both want a core get one each in turn, and being wrong costs speed — which is how nearly every fleet in the world is run. There is deliberately no setting for memory: a guest promised 8 GiB and handed 4 is not slow, it is killed.

Operation.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

OperationSpec.description: Something that could not finish inside a request. Done is computed from the target's own convergence, so an operation cannot disagree with the object it describes.

requestedBy.description: Derived: omitted, the API fills it in; stated, it must agree.

target.description: Derived: omitted, the API fills it in; stated, it must agree.

targetGeneration.description: Derived: omitted, the API fills it in; stated, it must agree.

verb.description: Derived: omitted, the API fills it in; stated, it must agree.

Pool.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

PoolSpec.description: Where volumes live. The spec is what an operator decided about a pool; the backend, the capacity and what is used are what its agent found.

accepting.description: Turning this off drains the pool: nothing new is provisioned into it, what it holds stays.

labels.description: What a volume's placement matches on.

Port.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

PortSpec.description: What an instance is attached to the fabric by. Programmed means the agent has it in its maps.

address.description: Left empty IPAM allocates one. It never changes afterwards — an address that moves under a running guest is an outage.

rateLimitMbit.description: Zero is unlimited. Multi-tenancy without a ceiling is one noisy neighbour away from an incident.

securityGroups.description: Rules only ever add allowances, so ordering does not matter and two groups cannot contradict each other. With none, the port keeps the platform's default: nothing in, everything out, replies always.

Project.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

ProjectSpec.description: The quota and access anchor. Usage is counted from what exists, never decremented by hand.

cell.description: Which cell this project's resources live in, and where requests for them are routed. Leave empty to use whichever cell answers — which is what an installation with one cell wants.

parent.description: The name of a `folders` object. Roles granted on the folder reach every project under it. Quota and policy are this project's own.

policy.customSizes.description: Whether guests here may be sized by typed numbers instead of a flavor. Only asked once the cell has flavors at all: with a menu defined, the closed answer is the sold one, and this is the deliberate exception for the customer whose shapes are their own. Settable at creation only.

policy.devicePassthrough.description: Whether guests here may be given a GPU or a NIC of their own. A passed-through device is a physical thing one guest holds and no other guest can have, so a project that may ask for them can empty a node of the hardware everybody else was scheduled against. Settable at creation only.

policy.floatingIps.description: Whether this project may claim addresses the world can reach. They come out of address space the cell was given by whoever is above it, so a project that could mint them could exhaust the pool every other project is waiting on. Settable at creation only.

policy.hostBridges.description: One bridge per line, as they are named on the nodes. A network put on one takes its guests off this platform's networks and onto whatever the machine is on — no address from us, no gateway, no security group. Empty means this project gets logical networks only, which is what a new customer should have. Named rather than a yes/no, because what anybody means by a host bridge is a particular wire. Settable at creation only.

quota.devices.description: Each one is a piece of hardware that exists once and cannot be oversubscribed, so without a cap one project can take every accelerator in the cell.

quota.floatingIps.description: An address that outlives the machine answering on it is scarce and externally routable.

quota.loadBalancers.description: Each one takes an address out of a subnet and datapath entries on every ingress host.

quota.volumes.description: A count, separate from the space: per-volume overhead is a different worry from capacity, and the two are capped apart.

Role.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

RoleSpec.description: The four rungs say how much somebody may do. A role here says *what* — collection by collection, for the case a rung cannot express: may restart the database machines, may not touch the network.

description.description: Somebody granting this will read this line and nothing else.

grants.description: A verb, and the collections it applies to. Being able to act on something carries being able to see it — anything else is a button that works above a screen that shows nothing.

Router.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

RouterSpec.description: Which of this project's networks reach each other. A membership rather than a box: there is nothing to place and nothing to fail over — the gateway answers on whichever machine the packet is already on.

networks.description: The networks whose subnets reach each other. A network belongs to at most one router.

SecurityGroup.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

SecurityGroupSpec.description: What a port is allowed to carry. Rules only add allowances — ingress is denied, egress is allowed and replies always come back, so a port in no group is not an open one.

rules.description: Every rule permits; none of them forbids. A group with no rules is a group that allows nothing extra, which is the platform's default anyway: nothing in, everything out, replies always.

Snapshot.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

SnapshotSchedule.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

SnapshotScheduleSpec.description: The cheap half of the pair. A snapshot lives in the volume's own pool — taken in a moment, costs almost nothing, and lost with the pool it is in. For a copy that survives losing the pool, use a backup schedule.

everyHours.description: Cheap enough to run hourly. A snapshot lives in the volume's own pool: it is the right tool for going back an hour, and it is lost with the pool — which is what backups are for.

keep.description: Only finished ones count, so a run of failures never expires the last one that worked. Snapshots taken by hand are never expired.

volume.description: The name of a `volumes` object. What is snapshotted.

SnapshotSpec.description: The console has no form for this collection, so its fields are not enumerated here; docs/rest-contract.md names them.

Status.description: The owning agent's report. `Unknown` is an honest absence of knowledge — there is no `PENDING` — and the rest of the shape is the agent's.

Subnet.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

SubnetSpec.description: A range on a network, and the count of what IPAM has handed out of it.

reserved.description: Addresses the platform will not hand out.

UsageRecord.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

UsageRecordSpec.description: What this project had, read once an hour and kept for ninety days. A reading is a sample, not a total: something created and destroyed between two of them is in neither. Quota says what is in use now; this is the only thing that remembers.

User.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

UserSpec.description: Who can sign in. A password is set from the row rather than shown on it — the platform stores a hash and cannot recover the original, which is the point.

cellAdmin.description: May do anything anywhere in this cell, including inside every project. Grant it to operate the platform, not to use it.

disabled.description: Ends every session this account holds immediately, and refuses new sign-ins. Its roles are kept, so turning it back on restores exactly what it had.

displayName.description: Shown on screen. Never used to decide anything — the account's id is its identity.

service.description: A program rather than a person: it signs in with no password and carries a token instead, minted by an operator and shown once. It is named in a project's bindings like anybody else and gets the same four roles.

Volume.description: What was asked for (`spec`), what is (`status`), and how far the second is behind the first (`meta.generation` against `status.observedGeneration`).

VolumeSpec.description: Block devices. A volume knows nothing about who has it open — that is an attachment.

encryptionKey.description: Empty means the bytes are stored in the clear, which is a decision rather than a default. Settable at creation only.

pool.description: Left empty, the cell chooses: the accepting pool with the most room. Naming one is for operators pinning a volume to specific hardware — a tenant cannot list pools and does not need to. Settable at creation only.

sourceImage.description: The name of a `images` object. Left empty the volume comes up blank. Settable at creation only.

sourceSnapshot.description: Restores that snapshot into a new volume. A volume is never restored in place, so this is what restoring means. Settable at creation only.

bearer.description: A session token from `POST /api/v1/sessions`, a service-account token from `POST /api/v1/users/{id}/tokens`, or a node's own credential.

info.description: The JSON gateway over the same handlers gRPC serves. A resource is addressed the way AIP addresses one — `projects/{project}/instances/{instance}` — and the HTTP path is that name under `/api/v1/`. Every resource body is `meta`, `spec` and `status`: what was asked for, and what the node that owns it reports. Only a controller writes spec; only the owning agent writes status; `generation` and `observedGeneration` say whether the second has caught up with the first. docs/rest-contract.md is the contract in prose; this document is derived from the router and the console's schema and cannot disagree with either.
